exercises.title: Dynamic Keyword Calls
exercises.description: Use Run Keyword to call keywords dynamically by name.
instructions: Use 'Run Keyword' to call the keyword stored in ${keyword_name}
The test should log the message
exercises.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Call
    # Write code here
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Call
    ${keyword_name}    Set Variable    Log
    Run Keyword    ${keyword_name}    Dynamic execution!
hints: Run Keyword executes a keyword by name
First argument is the keyword name
Remaining arguments are passed to the keyword
Useful for conditional execution

exercises.title: Conditional Keyword Execution
exercises.description: Use Run Keyword If to conditionally execute keywords.
instructions: Use 'Run Keyword If' to check if ${status} == 'active'
Use Run Keyword If    '${status}' == 'active'    Log    System is active
exercises.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
Conditional Execution
    # Write code here
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Conditional Execution
    ${status}    Set Variable    active
    Run Keyword If    '${status}' == 'active'    Log    System is active
hints: Run Keyword If takes condition and keyword
Condition must be in quotes for strings
Alternative to IF...END for simple cases
Can use ELSE with Run Keyword Unless

hints: [Timeout] prevents keyword from running too long
Place after keyword name, before other settings
Keyword fails if timeout exceeded
Can use: seconds, minutes, hours

exercises.title: Keyword with Default Arguments
exercises.description: Create keywords with multiple default argument values.
instructions: Call it three ways: no args, with host, with host and port
exercises.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
Test Defaults
    # Call keyword multiple ways

*** Keywords ***
# Define keyword with defaults
exercises.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Test Defaults
    Connect To Server
    Connect To Server    192.168.1.1
    Connect To Server    192.168.1.1    9090

*** Keywords ***
Connect To Server
    [Arguments]    ${host}=localhost    ${port}=8080    ${timeout}=30
    Log    Connecting to ${host}:${port} (timeout: ${timeout}s)
hints: Multiple defaults: ${arg1}=val1 ${arg2}=val2
Can provide 0 to N arguments
Defaults filled from left to right
Makes keywords flexible and reusable
